turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, show our young guest how games are played in Satis House.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. Estella, will you please show me?

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Observe, Pip, how the world passes us by, yet we remain frozen in time.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will observe.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Take care, Estella, that Pip learns well the lessons of this place.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham, I will learn well.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Pip, look around you. Let this room be a lesson in the folly of holding onto pain and the foolishness of a heart that trusts too easily.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham, I will look around and learn.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Observe the clocks, Pip. They are stopped at the hour of my betrayal, a testament to the time that has lost its meaning to me.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham, I see the clocks. They look strange, stopped like that.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Pip, do you see the withered flowers and the dust that settles where no one moves? This is what a heart left unloved becomes.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I see them, Miss Havisham. It looks very sad in here.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: And yet, I continue to wait, for a time that will never come. You, Pip, are here because I have a use for you.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I understand, Miss Havisham. I hope I can be of some help to you.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella shall show you your place, Pip. Observe well, for there are lessons in every corner of this house.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: Yes, Miss Havisham. I will do my best to learn and help.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I have no need for your pity, boy. My clock stops, but my heart does not.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I won't, Miss Havisham. I won't pity you or anyone else, but I will try to understand.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will see, Pip. This house is a mirror of my heart, frozen in time and filled with shadows.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there! with an impatient movement of the fingers of her right hand; play, play, play!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: So new to him, so old to me; so strange to him, so familiar to me; so melancholy to both of us! Call Estella.
